QQQ.source: Yahoo Finance via yfinance (unofficial provider client)

interpretation.text:
QQQ’s 252-return DFA H was 0.482 on Nov 20, near 0.5 for independent finite-variance returns. R²=0.928 measures fit only over scales 8–63. Short/long slopes (0.462/0.569) diverge: one line fits poorly across scales, suggesting possible crossover or a temporary volatility shift. Magnitude H=0.774 suggests stronger volatility clustering, not tradable predictability.

H rebounded from 0.455 Nov 13, up 0.018/0.027 over 1/5 observations. Its prior-30 standardized deviation (+0.165) isn’t a significance test because windows overlap.

Hill alpha rose from 3.198 Nov 5 to 3.499 Nov 19, then fell to 3.378 (1,000 returns; k=100; x_min=0.02046 in absolute log-return units). Lower/higher alpha suggests heavier/thinner tails if the model fits. The idealized independent-return standard error (0.338) understates uncertainty under dependence. The 5%/15% cutoffs give 3.419/2.985, not confidence bounds. Alpha can plateau when the largest returns don’t change. These are uncertain descriptive estimates, not a crash forecast.

SOXX.source: Yahoo Finance via yfinance (unofficial provider client)

interpretation.text:
On Nov. 20, SOXX’s 252-return DFA H was 0.437, below 0.5 for ideal independent, finite-variance returns. Despite R²=0.962 over scales 8–63, short/long slopes of 0.420/0.525 imply one line fits poorly across scales, possibly reflecting crossover. Magnitude H=0.778 suggests stronger volatility clustering, not tradable predictability.

H fell from 0.511 on Oct. 23 but rose 0.022/0.021 over the latest 1/5 observations. The prior-30 z-score was −0.86, not a significance test because windows overlap.

Hill alpha fell from 3.031 on Nov. 19 to 2.946, using 1,000 returns, k=99 and x_min=0.0390 absolute log-return units. Lower alpha suggests heavier tails if the model fits. The independent-sample SE of 0.296 understates uncertainty with dependence. The 5%/15% cutoffs yield 3.474/2.541, not confidence bounds. Alpha can plateau when new returns miss the top 99. These are uncertain descriptive estimates, not a crash forecast.

NVDA.source: Yahoo Finance via yfinance (unofficial provider client)

interpretation.text:
NVDA’s 252-return DFA H rose from 0.353 on Oct 12 to 0.562 on Nov 20, above the independent finite-variance reference of 0.5. R²=0.974 describes fit only at tested scales. Short and long slopes (0.490 versus 0.677) make one exponent a poor fit across scales 8–63, suggesting possible crossover. Magnitude H=0.676 suggests volatility clustering, not tradable predictability.

H rose 0.038 and 0.092 over one and five observations. It was 2.82 standard deviations above its prior-30 mean. With overlapping windows, this is not a significance test.

Hill alpha fell from 2.921 to 2.812 on those dates. Lower/higher means heavier/thinner tails if the model fits. The 1,000-return window uses 99 extremes from 0.04449 absolute log-return units. Independent-return SE=0.283 understates uncertainty under dependence. The 5%/15% cutoffs give 3.254/2.824, not a confidence interval. Unchanged extremes can produce plateaus. These are uncertain descriptive estimates, not a crash forecast.

SPY.source: Yahoo Finance via yfinance (unofficial provider client)

interpretation.text:
On Nov 20, SPY’s 252-return DFA H was 0.502, near the independent finite-variance reference of 0.5. R²=0.953 measures fit only on scales 8–63. Short/long slopes (0.472/0.572) differ enough that one line fits poorly across scales, suggesting possible crossover. Absolute-return H=0.717 suggests stronger persistence in volatility, not tradable predictability. H rose 0.020/0.021 over 1/5 observations. Its prior-30 z=+0.43 isn’t a significance test because windows overlap.

Hill alpha=3.294 uses 1,000 returns (~4 years), k=99, and x_min=0.01461 in absolute log-return units. Lower/higher alpha suggests heavier/thinner tails if the model fits. The idealized i.i.d. standard error, 0.331, understates uncertainty under dependence. The 5%/15% cutoffs give 3.223/2.877, not a confidence interval.

H/alpha rose from 0.448/3.252 (Oct 12) to 0.527/3.400 (Nov 6), then eased. Unchanged top extremes can explain alpha plateaus without implying a static market. These are uncertain descriptive estimates, not a crash forecast.
